justification: The text opens on the settled county rule — “Forty-four were in mixed-flow machines, which account for a third of the county’s drying capacity” and “The explanation is as settled as the count” — and then gives four paragraphs to Calverend, Grendisham and Tarrowfen disagreeing about the cause, which is exactly D. A is incidental only (“at so much per ton per point of moisture”); B is one strand of Grendisham’s objection (“nobody was there to see it early”), not the subject; C is never argued anywhere.

Verbatim: “His team swabbed the duct faces of twenty-six machines that had never burned; per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent.” That is equal dirtiness, so B. A is the reverse of the finding, C is never claimed, and D is contradicted by “The swabs are hard to walk past” — the writer treats the sample as decisive, not too small.

Grendisham’s point is that the second time in the file is a discovery time: “On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught.” That is C exactly. A is the opposite of “Set those two numbers side by side and of course the fire looks late”; B and D are never said — she attacks how the times are read, not their coverage or their purpose.

The stretch is defined by a commercial clock, not by equipment: “Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest, when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator’s delivery window is closing”, and Tarrowfen concludes “Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine, and the machine stops mattering.” The implication is A — the squeeze is the calendar and the contract, common to everyone drying, whatever machine they own. B is false on the arithmetic (forty-nine of sixty-one), C is an overreach nobody in the text claims, and D (grain arriving faster than dryers can take it) is not addressed.

The last paragraph rules on both halves: the old dirt explanation is finished — “The county’s standard advice rests on a difference in dirt that twenty-six machines failed to show, and nobody in the argument now defends it on the old ground” — while the replacement is unproved: “Until then Calverend’s account fits the evidence without having been tested by it.” That is C. A is wrong because she sustains Grendisham (“Grendisham’s objection has not been answered”); B is wrong because she plainly takes sides; D is the direct opposite of “without having been tested by it”.

Gap (1) completes a fixed idiom: “Whoever joins at the bottom is being asked, in the politest possible terms, to take the long ___.” “Take the long view” is the established collocation for accepting a distant payoff, and it fits the twelve-year wait (“which puts the bottom of the list twelve years from a key”). “Take the long outlook / gaze / sight” are all non-collocations in English, so C is the only defensible filler.

Gap (2) heads a sentence stating a formal rule that the paragraph then sets against practice: “___, a plot cannot be inherited”, followed by “That is the clause, and nobody disputes it. It is simply not what the list runs on.” “Strictly” (= strictly speaking) is precisely the hedge that flags rule-versus-reality, and the contrast is developed later in “The clause cannot reach what grows around it.” “Increasingly” implies a trend the text denies, “Curiously” marks a surprise the text does not present, and “Privately” contradicts a written, undisputed clause.

Gap (3) is a quoted idiom about advancement by bereavement: “The older hands have a phrase for this among themselves, about waiting for dead men’s ___. It is not affectionate and it is not quite a joke.” The English phrase is “dead men’s shoes”, and the context — movement on the list coming only when “somebody else stops”, including “a winter that settles it” — is exactly its meaning. Boots, coats and gloves are not the idiom.

Gap (4) sits inside a two-sided negation that brackets neutrality: “the tone of that line is not approving, but it is not ___ either.” The slot must therefore hold the opposite pole from “approving”, which is “censorious” (severely critical). “Gracious” lies on the same side as approving and makes the contrast collapse, while “cautious” and “anxious” name a temperament rather than the disapproval the minutes are being cleared of.

Gap (5) is about a rule left unused: “The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list. The rule has not been ___.” “Invoke” is the standard verb for calling a rule into effect, and the unused rule explains why “One name has stood at the top since 2019” after “Three times the answer was no”. Rules are not summoned, provoked or evoked; only C is idiomatic here.

The passage says height is the readable variable: “The can that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack, the flue from the attic bedroom, with the least warm air beneath it to do the lifting.” A flue that smoked is one drawing badly, so A. B is contradicted by the stated reason for narrowing (“since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening”), C by “Pattern tells you very little”, and D by “the pots seldom match” and “Yards sold whatever was in stock”.

The two hatches are open for very different lengths of time yet take almost the same traffic: “the chandler’s hatch opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller’s opened at two and took in 390. Both shut when the evening cart went at eight.” Thirteen hours against six for a difference of twenty-two letters implies the deadline, not the duration, is what fills the hatch — D. B is false on those numbers (390 is not “far” below 412), C reverses the dependence (the shops shut to suit the cart), and A attributes a motive the text never evidences — if the hourly allowance drove behaviour the bookseller would not have waited until two.

The sequence is stated directly: “Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten, när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan. Malmen grävdes upp i smala rutor, lades i högar på fastare mark och fick ligga ute vintern över”, and only then “Först därefter rostades den på en bädd av ved” — which is C. A inverts both the season and the order of roasting; B is contradicted by “Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt”; D is contradicted by “Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte.”

The trial result is explicit: “De blåsningar som drevs hårdast, med tätare bälgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet, och klumpen sprack under släggan i stället för att låta sig sträckas.” That is A, cause and effect included. B reverses the direction, C overstates it into “samtliga blåsningar misslyckades”, and D names an outcome (how to build and dry a furnace) the experiments are never said to have produced.

The text makes solid-state reduction the hinge of everything else: “Järnet reducerades i fast form… det som blev kvar bakades ihop till en klump som aldrig runnit någonstans”, then “Ur detta följer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom. En blåsning gav några kilo järn… Tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efteråt, i räckningen.” That is D — both lump size and where the labour sat. A overreaches to “varje bygd” against “Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt”; B’s “i alla stycken underlägsen” is refuted by Tolvsäter’s finding and by the hyttan’s own costs; C is contradicted by “uppteckningarna… säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen.”

The experiments reinterpret the same measurements: “den järnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lägre järnhalt blir trögflytande vid de temperaturer en sådan ugn orkar hålla… Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet.” That is B. A is Krokvall’s “dålig kontroll” reading, which the text says the trials speak against (“det är tolkningen av dem som försöken talar emot”); C is false since the figure is “i flera fall” and dating comes from “Kolet ur tappgroparna”; D is contradicted by “varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen.”

She withdraws her vote for the charge while keeping the need: “Nu vill jag ta tillbaka rösten” and “Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga”, ending with “Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten” — equipment yes, fee no, which is D. A is the opposite of taking the vote back; B is contradicted by the missing gear (“badstegen slutar en halvmeter ovanför vattenytan”, hjärtstartaren “2,3 kilometer bort”); C names a payer the text never proposes — she puts the cost on the operating budget, not on the förening.

The measured figure is the paid share: “Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna”, so roughly seven nights in ten went unpaid — A. C inverts the number; B is refuted by the fact that the municipality did measure it (“Kommunens egen uppföljning”); D is never mentioned — the sign, code and open gate are described as still in place.

The finding is hedged exactly as D states it: “Där skriften gick att jämföra med annat i mappen var yrkesordet i regel abonnentens eget.” B strips both qualifiers (“i regel” and the comparability condition) into “varje bevarad blankett” and so overstates the evidence; A is the opposite of that sentence; C is contradicted by “Titelraden var tom på den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista över godkända ord, ingen anvisning om längd.”

She drops the suspicion outright: “Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså. Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt, och den förklaring som från början låg närmast är också den som står kvar” — that closest explanation being “fåfänga”, the ordinary one, which is B. A contradicts “Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt”; the leftover puzzles (“Ett par saker får jag ändå inte att gå ihop”) are loose ends about individual entries, not a verdict that the question is undecidable (C) or that two mechanisms are both needed (D).

The passage states the timing and the order explicitly: "Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten, när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan. Malmen grävdes upp i smala rutor, lades i högar på fastare mark och fick ligga ute vintern över", and only then "Först därefter rostades den på en bädd av ved" — dig in late autumn, weather over winter, roast afterwards. A inverts both the season and the sequence (spring-winter digging, roasting before stacking); B is contradicted by "Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt"; D is contradicted by "Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte." Only C reproduces the text without adding or reversing anything.

The trial result is stated directly: "De blåsningar som drevs hårdast, med tätare bälgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet, och klumpen sprack under släggan" — harder driving produced a more brittle iron because carbon entered the metal. B reverses the direction of the effect; C's "samtliga blåsningar misslyckades" is an absolute the text never makes (the finding is about brittleness, not universal failure); D describes the drying and masonry of the furnace, which the passage presents as general background ("Innan den kunde fyllas måste den torkas långsamt") and not as a finding of the thirty-six blåsningar. A is the only option that matches both the cause and the effect reported.

The passage makes solid-state reduction the organising fact — "Det är hantverkets utgångspunkt. Järnet reducerades i fast form ... Ur detta följer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom" — and then names both consequences: a few kilos per blåsning, and "Tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efteråt, i räckningen". A overreaches to "varje bygd" when the text says "Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt"; B's "i alla stycken underlägsen" is exactly what Tolvsäter's experiments refute; C is contradicted by "uppteckningarna, som är utförliga om vem som ägde vad, säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen". D alone states a link the text itself draws.

Tolvsäter's second finding is stated as a condition, not a fault: "Och den järnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lägre järnhalt blir trögflytande vid de temperaturer en sådan ugn orkar hålla ... Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet." A is Krokvall's reading ("ett tecken på dålig kontroll"), which the passage says the experiments argue against; C is contradicted by "i flera fall kring en tredjedel av vikten" and by the fact that dating comes from charcoal ("Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket"); D is contradicted outright by "varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen". B is the only conclusion the text licenses.

The writer retracts her support for the charge while conceding the need: "Nu vill jag ta tillbaka rösten" and "Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga", closing with the alternative funding route "Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten". A is wrong because she rejects the charge rather than wanting it raised; B is contradicted by the catalogue of missing equipment ("en livboj vars lina någon har kapat", the ladder half a metre above the water, the defibrillator 2,3 km away); C names the wrong payer, since "driftsbudgeten" is the municipality's, not the association's. D states exactly her position: equipment yes, fee no.

The only figure given for the ställplats is "Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna", i.e. roughly seven nights in ten went unpaid. B is contradicted by the fact that the municipality did measure it and produced a number; C inverts the figure; D is not addressed anywhere — the sign is described as still part of the arrangement ("en skylt, en kod och tilliten till att gästen skannar"), with no mention of removal. A is the correct restatement of 31 percent paid.

The finding is hedged twice in the text and option D preserves both hedges: "Där skriften gick att jämföra med annat i mappen var yrkesordet i regel abonnentens eget." B drops the hedges and claims every preserved form, which the passage does not support (comparison was possible only for some, and only "i regel"); A is contradicted by the same sentence and by her conclusion "Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså"; C is contradicted by "Titelraden var tom på den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista över godkända ord, ingen anvisning om längd." D is the only faithful statement.

She abandons her suspicion explicitly: "Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså. Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt, och den förklaring som från början låg närmast är också den som står kvar" — and that nearest explanation was the ordinary one, "Den förklaring som ligger närmast är fåfänga." A is the opposite of "Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt"; C misreads the residual puzzles ("Ett par saker får jag ändå inte att gå ihop") as an inability to decide, when she has decided; D invents a synthesis the text never proposes, since she says all three of her mechanisms were absent. B is correct.

The text opens with the settled local rule — "Ask anyone in the county who dries grain for money which machine burns, and the answer comes back at once: the mixed-flow" — and then spends four paragraphs on competing accounts of why, from Calverend's timing to Grendisham's clock objection to Tarrowfen's "I would move it one step further out, to the contract". A is wrong because no drying price trend is traced across the nine harvests; B captures only Grendisham's single objection about unmanned sites, not the article; C is absent — nobody argues for small farms drying their own crop. D names both halves of the piece.

The swab result is stated plainly: "His team swabbed the duct faces of twenty-six machines that had never burned; per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent." A asserts the very difference the swabs failed to find; C is not addressed, since nothing is said about newest ducts being clean, and Grendisham's counter-example runs the other way ("buckets of fines out of ducts in February from machines that swabbed clean in September"); D is contradicted by the writer's own weighting, "The swabs are hard to walk past", which treats twenty-six machines as telling. B is the only supported reading.

Grendisham's objection is that the second timestamp is an observation time, not an ignition time: "The other time in the file is the moment the call came in. On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught ... It looks late because nobody was there to see it early." A is the opposite of her point, which is that the two numbers cannot be set side by side; B is not addressed — she disputes the meaning of the times, not the coverage of the log; D overstates, since she argues the times are misread rather than unusable as evidence. C is her argument.

Tarrowfen's point is that the calendar, not the equipment, is doing the work: "Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine, he argues, and the machine stops mattering. Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest, when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator's delivery window is closing." That pressure is described as a property of the tail of the season rather than of any machine type, which is what A states. B is contradicted by forty-nine of sixty-one; C is an outcome nobody claims, and Tarrowfen concedes the schedule "belongs to the elevators"; D is not addressed — trucks waiting is mentioned in the closing question, but no claim is made that arrivals outrun drying capacity.

The final paragraph splits the verdict exactly as C describes: the old dirt-based explanation is finished — "The county's standard advice rests on a difference in dirt that twenty-six machines failed to show, and nobody in the argument now defends it on the old ground" — while Calverend's replacement is unproved: "Grendisham's objection has not been answered ... Until then Calverend's account fits the evidence without having been tested by it." A misstates her position, since she endorses Grendisham's reading of the call records rather than calling them worthless; B is wrong because she does adjudicate rather than stay neutral; D is the direct opposite of "without having been tested by it".

The fixed English idiom is "take the long view", and the sentence is built for it: "Whoever joins at the bottom is being asked, in the politest possible terms, to take the long ___(1)___", after twelve years' wait has just been quantified. A gives "take the long outlook", which is not an English collocation; B and D produce "take the long gaze" and "take the long sight", both literal-visual and idiomatically dead. Only C yields the idiom the sentence's politeness formula depends on.

The paragraph sets a rule against a practice: "___(2)___, a plot cannot be inherited ... That is the clause, and nobody disputes it. It is simply not what the list runs on." That concessive structure requires "Strictly" — strictly speaking the rule says X, but in practice something else governs. A implies a trend over time, which contradicts a standing clause nobody disputes; C would mark the rule as surprising, but the text calls it undisputed; D is incoherent, since the clause is public and formal rather than private. B is the only adverb the contrast supports.

The set phrase is "waiting for dead men's shoes", and the text flags it as an idiom in use among a group: "The older hands have a phrase for this among themselves, about waiting for dead men's ___(3)___. It is not affectionate and it is not quite a joke." B, C and D are all plausible items of clothing but none forms an existing English expression, and the sentence's framing as a known phrase requires the fixed idiom rather than a fresh image. A is the only defensible fill.

The construction is a two-sided denial that needs opposite poles: "the tone of that line is not approving, but it is not ___(4)___ either" — the second term must sit on the disapproving end, which is "censorious". A fails because "gracious" lies on the same side as "approving", making the sentence redundant rather than balanced; B and C introduce a different axis entirely (caution, anxiety) and leave the "but ... either" frame without a contrast to close. D is the only option that completes the neither-warm-nor-hostile reading.

A rule is the standard object of "invoke": "The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list. The rule has not been ___(5)___" — i.e. nobody has applied it to the name that refused three times. A is a category error, since one summons a person, not a rule; B would mean the rule was goaded into existence, which is nonsense here; D is the near-miss trap, but "evoke" means to call up a feeling or memory, not to bring a rule into operation. C is the only correct collocation.

The passage states the reading directly: "Height is the part worth reading. The can that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack." B is contradicted by the stated reason for a narrow mouth — "since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening" — which is draught, not rain or birds; C is contradicted by "Pattern tells you very little"; D is contradicted by "the pots seldom match" and by the account of yards selling "whatever was in stock". A is the only supported statement.

The numbers are set up to be compared: the chandler's "opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller's opened at two and took in 390", and "Both shut when the evening cart went at eight" — thirteen hours against six produced almost the same count, so what governed the traffic was the departure deadline rather than the length of opening. B is the arithmetic trap: 412 against 390 is not "far more". C reverses the dependency, since the shops shut to suit the cart. A attributes a motive the text does not support and the bookseller's two o'clock opening actively undercuts: if keepers were padding hours for the threepence, the bookseller would not have opened late. D is the implication the figures carry.
